title: Introduce staged compatibility advisory and runtime probe requirements for new open-model onboarding
creator: Samantha Lee
description: Clarify product requirements and acceptance criteria for a staged 'compatibility advisory' that accompanies every new open-model entry into the Redwood model catalog. The advisory combines automated static checks and short runtime probe jobs to generate a triage-level verdict (Green/Yellow/Red) plus structured notes that inform pinning recommendations, fallback mappings, and rollout guardrails. This ticket defines scope, concrete checks, telemetry signals, test plan, and rollout steps; captures trade-offs and open questions for engineering and security; and lists explicit acceptance criteria for shipping a first-pass advisory pipeline and UI surface in the catalog entry page.
scope_included: Static metadata validations: tokenizer compatibility, model architecture family, param count reporting, declared quantization support
Lightweight runtime probes: 100 short inference requests (variable length prompts) run on dedicated probe workers across CPU and GPU variants
Automated advisory synthesis: compute a compatibility score and label (Green/Yellow/Red) with structured notes and recommended pin/fallback variants
Catalog UI surface: show advisory label + top 3 structured notes and a telemetry link on the model detail page
Acceptance test harness: deterministic fixture runs and synthetic prompts to validate probe outputs
scope_excluded: Full-scale production performance benchmarks (throughput/latency p99) — tracked in a follow-up
Auto-quantization of models or in-place weight modifications
Customer-facing API changes to routing/fallback behavior (those require separate runtime rollout tickets)
acceptance_criteria: All new open-model catalog entries trigger static validations and runtime probe jobs on intake (probe completes within 30 minutes for models < 20B params)
Advisory labels are computed deterministically from probe + static checks and displayed on the model detail page within the catalog UI
Pinning recommendation field is populated: either 'Pin recommended', 'Soft pin', or 'No pin', with justification text derived from checks
Runtime probes exercise tokenization edge cases and KV cache basic flows; failure modes are captured as structured notes (e.g., tokenization mismatch, OOM on GPU-48Gi, missing model artifacts)
False positive rate for 'Red' advisories on a held-out dataset of 120 community models is < 6% and false negative rate for severe incompatibility is < 4%
Automated advisory generation includes at least 3 telemetry signals (probe success rate, median probe latency, mem headroom estimate) and they are ingested into the catalog metrics dashboard
Security review signoff completed and no blocked security findings remain
Engineering implementation has unit/integration tests and an initial GitHub PR merged with the probe runner and advisory synthesizer behind a feature flag
test_plan: Unit tests for static validation rules (tokenizer detection, declared format checks)
Integration test: trigger intake for 10 synthetic models with known issues and assert advisory labels match expected
Probe runner smoke test on staging: run probes on 20 community models spanning 1B-30B params
Canary UI rollout: show advisory on 5% of user sessions in staging, validate render and link to telemetry dashboard
Regression test: measure false positive/negative rates on historical model set and log results to the QA dashboard
rollout_steps: Develop probe runner and static validators behind feature flag (ENG)
Create advisory synthesizer service and wire to catalog ingest pipeline (ENG)
Add catalog UI tile and telemetry link; hide by default behind feature flag (DES/Frontend)
Run staging campaign: intake 200 models and compare advisory outputs to manual auditor reviews (PM + Research)
Adjust thresholds and rule weights based on staging results; update acceptance criteria if needed
Feature-flagged production rollout at 5% of ingests for two weeks, monitor telemetry signals and manual audits
Increase to 25% if metrics stable, then full rollout; publish post-launch notes for customers
tradeoffs: Automated probes add latency to the intake pipeline; we accept probe completion within 30 minutes to balance thoroughness and TTV
Conservative 'Red' labeling reduces onboarding speed for some community models; to mitigate we include structured notes and a human review fast-path
Keeping the advisory logic simple reduces engineering complexity but may miss nuanced failure modes; iterative improvements planned based on telemetry
